title: 1953 AHSME Problem 37
statement: The base of an isosceles triangle is \(6\) inches and one of the equal sides is \(12\) inches. The radius of the circle through the vertices of the triangle is:

solutions.text:
The altitude is \[ \sqrt{12^2-3^2}=3\sqrt{15}, \] so the area is \(K=\tfrac12(6)(3\sqrt{15})=9\sqrt{15}.\) Hence the circumradius is \[ R=\frac{(12)(12)(6)}{4(9\sqrt{15})} =\frac{8\sqrt{15}}5. \] This value is not listed.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Drop the altitude to split the base into two segments of length \(3\)
